subject: CAIQ: control ancestry trace + artifact chronicle request
messages:
From: security@orchidbank.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ control ancestry / artifact chronicle request

Hi Marissa,

OrchidBank's SOC/CSA team is preparing for a targeted assessment focused on change provenance and control lineage for a subset of CAIQ controls (primarily CCM:SCM, DAT, LOG categories). Can you send us: 
- a short description of how Redwood maps CAIQ controls back to runtime artifacts (what we call "control ancestry")
- an example artifact chronicle for one control (e.g., how a config change flows to an audit log sample, including timestamps and S3/object IDs)
- a small sample of runtime telemetry (redacted) that demonstrates KV/cache invalidation tied to a deployment event

Preferably as: a single zip with a diagram, a short CSV mapping, and a log snippet. Our window is the week of Dec 7 — can you confirm availability and an expected delivery date?

Thanks,
Mike Hansen
Lead SOC Engineer
OrchidBank
attachments: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: security@orchidbank.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control ancestry / artifact chronicle request

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to provide a focused package that demonstrates our control-to-artifact trace for the requested categories. Plan below and gaps we need to close: 

Plan (deliver by Dec 9):
- Artifact chronicle (diagram + CSV) for CCM:LOG-1 example (log capture from deployment -> ingestion -> archival).
- Redacted KV-cache sample tied to a deployment event (timestamps + object refs).
- Short narrative (500–700 words) describing our mapping approach and chain-of-custody controls.

Open items for OrchidBank:
- Can you confirm the acceptable redaction policy (full UUIDs vs truncated IDs)? We typically provide truncated object IDs (first 8 chars) plus CloudTrail event ids.
- Any preference for CSV columns? We normally include: control_id, artifact_type, artifact_id, owner, retention_bucket, sample_link.

cc: Kimberly and Jordan — Kimberly, Jordan: can you own artifact extraction and produce the diagram + CSV respectively? I'll coordinate redaction and packaging.

Marissa
Sr. Security PM | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control ancestry / artifact chronicle request

Marissa / Mike — attaching first-pass artifacts for review. Files included: control-ancestry-diagram.png, caiq-crosswalk-extract.csv, sample-kv-cache-log.txt (redacted). Highlights and notes: 

- control-ancestry-diagram.png: shows control mapping from CAIQ claim -> internal control id (redwood-ctrl-173) -> pipeline step (deploy-service) -> telemetry sink (log-collector) -> archival bucket (rbx-logs-prod).
- caiq-crosswalk-extract.csv: includes mapping rows for three controls (CCM:LOG-1, CCM:DAT-3, CCM:SCM-2) with columns you requested.
- sample-kv-cache-log.txt: contains a 10-line snippet around a deployment event (2026-11-12T03:15:21Z) with object refs replaced by first-8 characters per your proposed redaction standard.

Notes / asks to OrchidBank: 
1) We replaced full UUIDs with the first 8 chars; if you need full IDs for subpoena/audit use, we'll prepare a stronger access plan under NDA.
2) The CSV contains internal owner usernames; we've changed those to role tags (e.g., infra-oncall) — flag if you need the real names for your traceability matrix.

I'll wait for your permission to finalize the archive by Dec 9.

-Kim
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: control-ancestry-diagram.png, caiq-crosswalk-extract.csv, sample-kv-cache-log.txt

- Redaction policy: first-8 chars are acceptable for our initial review. We will request full identifiers under a narrow evidence-only access policy if the auditor requires it.
- CSV: role tags are fine for now. If we get to a formal attestation step, we will ask for names tied to signoff windows.

Please go ahead and finalize the zip by Dec 9. Also, include a short note in the archive about timezones for timestamps (all logs are UTC).

Thanks — Mike
